purpose: Ozanimod is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults, helping to reduce the number of flare-ups and slow down disability. It is also used to treat moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in adults when other treatments have not worked well enough. It helps calm the immune system so it causes less damage to your body.
how_it_works: Your immune system has cells called lymphocytes that can sometimes attack your own body by mistake. Ozanimod works by trapping many of these harmful immune cells in your lymph nodes, so fewer of them travel through your bloodstream to cause damage. Think of it like keeping troublemakers from leaving a room so they cannot cause problems elsewhere in your body.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections like colds or nasal congestion, headache, increased blood pressure, urinary tract infections, back pain, elevated liver enzyme levels, and a slow heart rate especially when you first start the medication.
warnings: Before starting this medicine, your doctor will check your heart, as it can slow your heart rate, especially with your first dose. It can lower your immune system, making it harder to fight infections, so tell your doctor about any signs of infection. It may cause serious eye problems, liver damage, or increased blood pressure. Do not take it if you have had a heart attack, stroke, or certain heart rhythm problems in the last 6 months. It can harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control if you can become pregnant. You should not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: You start with a low dose of 0.23 mg by mouth once daily for the first 7 days, then increase to 0.46 mg once daily for days 8 through 14, and then move to the full maintenance dose of 0.92 mg once daily from day 15 onward. This gradual start-up helps your body adjust and reduces the chance of heart-related side effects. Take it at the same time each day, with or without food.
